boards.name: Durham City Council
boards.regular_schedule: 1st & 3rd Mondays at 7:00 PM (Work Sessions on Thursdays)

terms.label: 2025–2027 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 1, 2025 municipal election swearing-in: Mayor Leonardo Williams re-elected; Chelsea Cook elected to a full Ward 3 term; Matt Kopac (Ward 1, defeating DeDreana Freeman) and Shanetta Burris (Ward 2, defeating Mark-Anthony Middleton) sworn in; Javiera Caballero elected Mayor Pro Tempore.

terms.label: 2023–2025 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 4, 2023 municipal election swearing-in: Leonardo Williams sworn in as Mayor (succeeding retiring Elaine O'Neal and vacating Ward 3); Javiera Caballero re-elected At-Large; Nate Baker and Carl Rist sworn in At-Large (succeeding retiring Jillian Johnson and Monique Holsey-Hyman); Mark-Anthony Middleton continued as Mayor Pro Tempore. Chelsea Cook selected by Council on January 16, 2024 and sworn in on January 17, 2024 to fill the Ward 3 seat vacated when Leonardo Williams became Mayor.

terms.label: 2021–2023 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 6, 2021 municipal election swearing-in: Elaine O'Neal sworn in as Durham's first Black female Mayor (succeeding retiring Steve Schewel); Leonardo Williams sworn in for Ward 3 (succeeding Pierce Freelon); DeDreana Freeman (Ward 1) and Mark-Anthony Middleton (Ward 2) re-elected, with Middleton elected Mayor Pro Tempore. At-Large Council Member Charlie Reece resigned effective after his final council meeting on March 7, 2022 to relocate to Paris with his family, leaving a 6-member council while applicants were reviewed. Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman unanimously appointed and sworn in on May 12, 2022 to fill the At-Large seat vacated by Charlie Reece's resignation.

terms.label: 2019–2021 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 2, 2019 municipal election swearing-in: Mayor Steve Schewel and At-Large incumbents Jillian Johnson (Mayor Pro Tempore), Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero all re-elected and sworn in for new terms. Ward 3 Council Member Vernetta Alston resigned effective April 9, 2020 upon appointment by Gov. Roy Cooper to NC House District 29 (succeeding the late Rep. MaryAnn Black), leaving a 6-member council for nearly five months during the COVID-19 pandemic. Pierce Freelon appointed in a 4-2 special-meeting vote on August 31, 2020 (ceremonially sworn in September 4, 2020) to complete the remainder of Vernetta Alston's Ward 3 term.

terms.label: 2017–2019 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 4, 2017 municipal election swearing-in: Steve Schewel sworn in as Mayor (succeeding retiring 16-year Mayor Bill Bell and vacating his At-Large seat); DeDreana Freeman (Ward 1, succeeding retiring Cora Cole-McFadden), Mark-Anthony Middleton (Ward 2, succeeding retiring Eddie Davis), and Vernetta Alston (Ward 3, succeeding Don Moffitt) sworn in; Jillian Johnson elected Mayor Pro Tempore. Javiera Caballero appointed (5-1) and sworn in on January 16, 2018 to fill Mayor Steve Schewel's vacated At-Large seat, becoming the first Latina member of Durham City Council.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2015–2017 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 7, 2015 municipal election swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell and Steve Schewel (At-Large) re-elected; Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece sworn in At-Large replacing retiring 12-year incumbents Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2013–2015 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 2, 2013 municipal election swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (Ward 1), and Don Moffitt (Ward 3) re-elected/elected to full terms; Eddie Davis sworn in for Ward 2 succeeding retiring 30-year veteran Howard Clement III.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2011–2013 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 5, 2011 municipal election swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell and At-Large incumbents Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti re-elected; Steve Schewel sworn in At-Large replacing retiring Farad Ali. Ward 3 Council Member Mike Woodard resigned effective December 31, 2012 upon taking office in the North Carolina Senate, leaving a brief 6-member transition until Don Moffitt was seated on January 7, 2013. Don Moffitt appointed and seated on January 7, 2013 to complete the unexpired Ward 3 term of Mike Woodard.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2009–2011 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 7, 2009 municipal swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell and Ward incumbents Cora Cole-McFadden (Ward 1, Mayor Pro Tempore), Howard Clement III (Ward 2), and Mike Woodard (Ward 3) re-elected alongside At-Large members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2007–2009 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 3, 2007 municipal swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell re-elected (defeating Thomas Stith III); Farad Ali sworn in At-Large replacing Stith alongside re-elected At-Large members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti and Ward members Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard.
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive pre-2020 includes Regular Meetings only (Work Sessions archived starting 2020)

terms.label: 2005–2007 City Council
terms.transition_reason: December 2005 municipal swearing-in: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (Ward 1), Howard Clement III (Ward 2), Mike Woodard (Ward 3), and At-Large members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Thomas Stith III (Granicus archive begins Dec 2006).

terms.label: 2024–2028 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of the 2024–2028 Board on December 2, 2024 following the November 5, 2024 county-wide election. Newly elected commissioners Dr. Mike Lee, Michelle Burton, and Stephen Valentine joined returning incumbents Nida Allam and Wendy Jacobs, succeeding outgoing commissioners Brenda A. Howerton, Heidi Carter, and Nimasheena Burns. Annual Chair/Vice Chair rotation: Dec 2, 2024–Nov 30, 2025 Nida Allam (Chair) and Dr. Mike Lee (Vice Chair); Dec 1, 2025–present Dr. Mike Lee (Chair) and Nida Allam (Vice Chair).

terms.label: 2020–2024 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of Durham County's historic first all-female Board on December 7, 2020 following the November 3, 2020 election. Newly elected commissioners Nida Allam and Nimasheena Burns joined returning incumbents Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Heidi Carter, succeeding retiring 32-year veteran Ellen W. Reckhow and outgoing Vice Chair James Hill. Annual Chair/Vice Chair rotation: Dec 7, 2020–Dec 3, 2023 Brenda A. Howerton (Chair) and Wendy Jacobs (Vice Chair); Dec 4, 2023–Dec 1, 2024 Nida Allam (Chair) and Nimasheena Burns (Vice Chair).

terms.label: 2016–2020 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of the 2016–2020 Board on December 5, 2016 following the November 8, 2016 election. Newly elected commissioners Heidi Carter and James Hill joined returning incumbents Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton, succeeding outgoing commissioners Michael D. Page and Fred Foster Jr. Annual Chair/Vice Chair leadership remained consistent throughout the term: Wendy Jacobs (Chair, Dec 2016–Dec 2020) and James Hill (Vice Chair, Dec 2016–Dec 2020).
terms.coverage_note: YouTube archive starts Mar 2018 and includes Regular Sessions only (Work Sessions archived from Dec 2020)

terms.label: 2012–2016 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of the 2012–2016 Board on December 3, 2012 following the November 6, 2012 election. Newly elected commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Fred Foster Jr. joined returning incumbents Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton, as interim appointees Pam H. Karriker and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. concluded their service. Annual Chair/Vice Chair rotation: Dec 10, 2012–Dec 1, 2013 Fred Foster Jr. (Chair) and Brenda A. Howerton (Vice Chair); Dec 2, 2013–Dec 4, 2016 Michael D. Page (Chair) and Brenda A. Howerton (Vice Chair).

terms.label: 2008–2012 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of the 2008–2012 Board on December 1, 2008: Michael D. Page (Chair), Ellen W. Reckhow (Vice Chair), Becky M. Heron, Joe W. Bowser, and newly elected Brenda A. Howerton (succeeding Lewis Cheek and Philip Cousin Jr.), serving until Becky Heron's August 2011 resignation. Appointment of Pam H. Karriker in September 2011 to fill the unexpired term of longtime Commissioner Becky M. Heron (who resigned in August 2011 due to health), serving through Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's May 9, 2012 resignation. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser submitted his resignation on May 9, 2012 (formally accepted by the Board on May 14, 2012), creating a four-member voting board until Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. (unanimously appointed June 25, 2012 after the FY2012–13 budget vote) was seated at the July 23, 2012 regular session. Michael D. Page served as Chair and Ellen W. Reckhow as Vice Chair. Seating of interim appointee Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. at the July 23, 2012 regular session (the Board's sole July 2012 meeting), following his unanimous appointment on June 25, 2012 to fill the unexpired term of resigned commissioner Joe W. Bowser through December 2012. Michael D. Page served as Chair and Ellen W. Reckhow as Vice Chair.

terms.label: 2004–2008 Board of County Commissioners
terms.transition_reason: 2004–2008 Board (Durham County's first four-year BOCC term): Ellen W. Reckhow (Chair), Becky M. Heron (Vice Chair), Lewis A. Cheek, Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Michael D. Page (Granicus archive begins Dec 2006).

boards.name: Durham Public Schools Board of Education

terms.label: 2026–2028 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in on July 6, 2026 of March 3, 2026 election winners (all four DAE-endorsed): Natalie Bent Kitaif (District 1, succeeding Emily Chávez), Nadeen Bir (District 2, defeating incumbent Chair Bettina Umstead), Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero (District 3, succeeding Jessica Carda-Auten), and returning board member Xavier Cason (District 4, succeeding retiring 16-year incumbent Natalie Beyer). Joy Harrell-Goff elected Chair; Xavier Cason elected Vice Chair.

terms.label: 2024–2026 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in on July 1, 2024 of March 5, 2024 election winners: Joy Harrell-Goff (At-Large, succeeding Alexandra Valladares), Wendell Tabb (Consolidated District A, succeeding Jovonia Lewis), re-elected Millicent Rogers (Consolidated District B), and District 3 special election winner Jessica Carda-Auten. Millicent Rogers served as Chair and Jessica Carda-Auten as Vice Chair in 2024–2025; on July 8, 2025, Bettina Umstead was elected Chair and Millicent Rogers Vice Chair for 2025–2026.

terms.label: 2022–2024 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of May 17, 2022 election winners: Emily Chávez (District 1, succeeding outgoing two-term incumbent Mike Lee), Millicent Rogers (Consolidated District B special election, defeating appointed incumbent Frederick Xavier Ravin III), and re-elected incumbents Bettina Umstead (District 2), Matt Sears (District 3), and Natalie Beyer (District 4). Bettina Umstead continued as Chair; Matt Sears elected Vice Chair. Mid-term resignation of District 3 member and Vice Chair Matt Sears (announced January 31, 2023 to join the Durham Public Schools Foundation as Director of Partnerships), leaving a 6-member board pending appointment of a successor. Appointment (March 16, 2023) and swearing-in (March 23, 2023) of Jessica Carda-Auten to fill the District 3 vacancy left by Matt Sears, restoring the 7-member board. Bettina Umstead continued as Chair; Emily Chávez elected Vice Chair for 2023–2024.

terms.label: 2020–2022 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of March 3, 2020 election winners Alexandra Valladares (At-Large, defeating incumbent Steve Unruhe) and Jovonia Lewis (Consolidated District A, succeeding retiring 16-year member Minnie Forte-Brown). Consolidated District B incumbent Xavier Cason won re-election in March 2020 but resigned in June 2020 prior to taking the new term to join the Durham Public Schools Foundation, leaving a 6-member board. Bettina Umstead elected Chair; Mike Lee elected Vice Chair. Appointment and swearing-in of Frederick Xavier Ravin III on September 10, 2020 to fill the Consolidated District B vacancy left by Xavier Cason's resignation, restoring the 7-member board. Bettina Umstead served as Chair; Mike Lee (2020–2021) and Jovonia Lewis (2021–2022) served as Vice Chair.

terms.label: 2018–2020 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in following May 8, 2018 elections in which all four District 1–4 incumbents won full 4-year terms: Mike Lee (District 1), Bettina Umstead (District 2, first elected term after 2016 appointment), Matt Sears (District 3), and Natalie Beyer (District 4). Mike Lee continued as Chair; Steve Unruhe (2018–2019) and Bettina Umstead (2019–2020) served as Vice Chair.

terms.label: 2016–2018 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of March 15, 2016 election winners: Steve Unruhe (At-Large, succeeding retiring Leigh Bordley), Xavier Cason (Consolidated District B, succeeding outgoing Chair Heidi Carter who ran for Durham Board of County Commissioners), and unopposed incumbent Minnie Forte-Brown (Consolidated District A). Mike Lee elected Chair; Natalie Beyer elected Vice Chair. Mid-term resignation of District 2 member Sendolo Diaminah in late August 2016 amid meeting attendance scrutiny (triggering a 60-day statutory appointment window ending October 24, 2016), leaving a 6-member board while 11 applicants were vetted. Unanimous appointment and swearing-in of Bettina Umstead on October 5, 2016 to fill the unexpired District 2 term of Sendolo Diaminah, restoring the 7-member board. Mike Lee served as Chair; Natalie Beyer served as Vice Chair.

terms.label: 2014–2016 School Board
terms.transition_reason: Swearing-in of May 2014 election winners Dr. Mike Lee (District 1), Sendolo Diaminah (District 2), and Matt Sears (District 3) alongside returning members Heidi Carter (Chair), Minnie Forte-Brown (Vice Chair 2014–15), Natalie Beyer (District 4), and Leigh Bordley (At-Large). Coverage via official approved Board Minutes PDFs.

terms.label: 2012–2014 School Board
terms.transition_reason: 2012–2014 Board of Education: Heidi Carter (Chair, Consolidated District B), Minnie Forte-Brown (Vice Chair, Consolidated District A), Natalie Beyer (District 4), Leigh Bordley (At-Large), Nancy Cox (District 3), Fredrick A. Davis (District 2), and Omega Curtis Parker (District 1). Coverage begins Aug 2013 via YouTube recordings & official Board Minutes PDFs.
